speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: Have you experienced any episodes of unexplained fever, or do you feel a sensation of itching over your skin? I am trying to determine if this is truly Hodgkin lymphoma or another B-cell malignancy.

speaker: Patient
text: I noticed swelling in my neck over the last few days. It does not hurt, but it feels enlarged and fixed.

speaker: Doctor
text: The fixed, painless nature of the node combined with your B symptoms strongly suggests a malignant process, likely lymphoma. I need to know if you have experienced any pain in the enlarged lymph nodes after drinking alcohol, which is a rare but specific sign of Hodgkin lymphoma.

speaker: Patient
text: I also feel fullness in my abdomen and my clothes feel tighter. I do not have cough or recent travel.

speaker: Doctor
text: The abdominal fullness suggests significant splenomegaly or intra-abdominal lymphadenopathy, which contradicts the normal PET scan and raises suspicion for a leukemic phase or a different pathology. I need to assess your blood counts to see if there is peripheral involvement or bone marrow infiltration. REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count_with_Differential

speaker: Measurement

speaker: Doctor
text: The elevated white blood cell count with anemia suggests significant marrow infiltration or a leukemic phase, which explains the discrepancy with the PET scan. I need to examine the morphology of these circulating cells to distinguish between lymphoma and leukemia. REQUEST TEST: Peripheral_Blood_Smear

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal peripheral smear rules out leukemic involvement, so the elevated WBC is likely a reactive phenomenon rather than malignancy in the blood. I must request a repeat review of the lymph node biopsy images to ensure the initial diagnosis of CD20+ lymphoma is correct and to look for specific morphological features like Reed-Sternberg cells that might have been missed. speaker: Patient
text: I have smoked about one pack a day for many years, and I drink socially. The abdominal discomfort and fatigue have both been getting worse.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of B symptoms, widespread lymphadenopathy, and a CD20-positive biopsy confirms a B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma, likely Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma, despite the conflicting imaging results which may represent a technical error or early-stage disease not yet fully metabolically active on PET.
